chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Rene Hall's warnings about the deep South and the arranging-for-trombone deal
summary: Rene warns Fields that the deep South differs from Oklahoma; they agree he will teach Fields arranging for lessons in guitar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: While we're talking about Rene, he began to work around and everything, and he was just watching me, and so one day he said to me, I sure don't want to go down South with you,

and I always was a person that would ask questions and I said why, Rene? He said well you're talking to white folk. I said, am I wrong? He said, no you're not wrong, but you've just been around this area, this may be the South, but it's a lot different in the deep South. You're not supposed to be right with them, you've got to be agreeing with what they're doing. And so we just took that in and went on.

I guess it was maybe a couple of years, I didn't get any booking down in the deep South, but he was writing arrangements and everybody was just tickled over it and I said, I sure wish I could play the guitar. He said I'll tell you what, I'll make you a deal, you teach me guitar and where you're always telling me how you want somthing arranged and I'll teach you arrangement--you teach me trombone. And so I said that's a deal, and I guess that I lasted maybe about three months, but Rene would continue on. He said we made that deal and I'm ready for my lesson.
